title: OAAP app manifest (oaap-app.yaml), manifest versions 0.1, 0.2 and 0.4 (0.3 not yet covered)
$comment: This schema is an AUTHORING tool: it rejects unknown fields so a typo is caught where it is made. A node in the field reads more tolerantly (RFC-0012 §8.2) — it accepts a higher minor version and ignores what it does not know, because otherwise every extension of the format would be a flag day for the whole fleet. Strict schema, tolerant runtime. The newest schema always validates every manifest version still readable, which is why this one lists 0.1, 0.2 and 0.4 — 0.3 is a pre-existing gap (see the oaap_manifest property comment), not fixed by this change.

allOf.$comment: A field added in 0.2 may only be used by a manifest that declares 0.2. The runtime does NOT enforce this — it reads whatever it finds — but an author who uses a new field while still claiming the old version has made a mistake worth catching here.

Same rule as above, for the 0.4 field: 'launchpad' may only be used by a manifest declaring at least 0.4 (RFC-0036). Written against 0.1/0.2 only, because 0.3 (data_model/contributes/consumes, RFC-0031 Schritt 2) is not yet in the oaap_manifest enum below — a pre-existing gap in this authoring schema, tracked separately from this RFC's own change, not fixed here.

oaap_manifest.$comment: MAJOR.MINOR. A new MINOR only adds; a new MAJOR is the only thing a node may refuse (RFC-0012 §8.2). Deliberately not the semver 0.x reading, where the minor would carry breaking changes. 0.2 adds app.class. 0.4 adds the 'launchpad' section (RFC-0036). 0.3 (data_model/contributes/consumes, RFC-0031 Schritt 2) is intentionally NOT listed yet — this authoring schema was never updated for it; a manifest declaring 0.3 is valid at runtime (appctl.py) but not yet accepted here. Do not author a 0.3 manifest against this schema until that gap is closed.

must_understand.$comment: RFC-0012 §8.2 rule 2: features a reader MUST understand to handle this manifest correctly. A reader missing one refuses this app with a clear message instead of installing something half-understood — the exception that makes 'ignore what you do not know' safe. Only use it where ignoring the feature would produce a broken install; optional additions do not belong here.

class.$comment: Manifest 0.2, RFC-0012 §1.2. What the app IS, as opposed to app.type, which says how it is PACKAGED. 'frontend' (the default when absent) has a user interface; 'service' is used by other software and therefore gets no launchpad tile (oaap.apps.runtime 2.10). It belongs in the manifest and not only in a store list, because a node must be able to answer the question offline, for an app installed straight from Git, and without a foreign list being able to change what its launchpad shows. Deliberately NOT a must_understand feature: a node that ignores it shows one tile too many, which is untidy, not broken.

multiline.description: The value is a LIST. The portal offers one line per entry; on the wire the lines are joined with ';' — so an app parses the single-line form and no entry may itself contain ';'.

generate.description: Only for a key whose value THIS app defines: the portal offers to produce it, as 32 random bytes in url-safe base64 (alphabet [A-Za-z0-9_-], no padding) — a value the platform's line-based env file and ';'-separated lists can carry. Do NOT declare it on a key that holds somebody else's credential.

launchpad.description: Manifest 0.4, RFC-0036 D1/D2: developer hints about the launchpad tile's DISPLAY, never about who may see it (that stays 'routes[].roles' and the operator-set 'visibility', RFC-0007). Not 'placement' above — that section is node PLACEMENT per RFC-0003 (GPU, site), an unrelated meaning of the same English word.

group.description: An optional section label; tiles sharing one are shown under one heading on the launchpad. Absent means the pre-existing, unlabelled section.

embeddable.description: Reserved; has no effect yet (RFC-0036 D1). Every tile opens its app as a standalone page today, per RFC-0016's network isolation. The name is reserved now so a future embedded shell mode needs no breaking manifest change.

endpoints.description: RFC-0016/RFC-0015: at most one non-HTTP endpoint the app may declare; published only after an operator grants it on an 'exposed' node.

wish.description: desired published host port; granted if free, otherwise the platform assigns another (ignored when fixed:true, where container_port IS the port)

fixed.description: RFC-0017 §5.1: the port is a requirement, not a wish. Used by servers that advertise their own port to clients (a media server: ICE candidates carry the exact port). When true the endpoint is published unchanged (host_port == container_port), container_port MUST be in 8200-8299, and a grant fails loudly if the port is taken rather than reassigning.

reason.description: Why this app needs a port past the gateway. Required, because the operator granting it reads this sentence and nothing else — and the schema listed it as required without ever allowing it, so no manifest with an endpoint could validate (found 2026-08-24).
